title: Compounding Garden
blurb: Grow two gardens side by side and see why interest on interest, and starting early, change everything.
t1.title: Two gardens
t1.hook: Asha has two mango gardens. In one, the trees only give fruit. In the other, the fruit grows into new trees. Your mission: see which garden wins.
t1.define: **Simple interest** is earned only on your original money. **Compound interest** is earned on your original money and on the interest it already earned.
t1.analogy: In the simple garden, the same trees give fruit every year. In the compound garden, each year's fruit grows into more trees that give fruit too.
q1.prompt: In which garden does the fruit grow new trees?
q1.fb.b: In the simple garden the same trees give fruit each year. Interest does not earn more interest there.
q1.explain: In the compound garden, interest earns interest, like fruit growing into new trees.
q2.opt.b: Your original money and earlier interest
q2.hint: Reread the definition at the top of this task.
q2.explain: Simple interest is earned only on the original amount.
t2.title: Guess the garden
t2.define: Compound interest looks slow at first, then speeds up. Your guess will show how well your instinct fits the maths.
t2.predict: A compound garden starts with {P} at {rate} a year. What will it be worth after {yrs} years?
t2.reveal: Each year's interest earns interest too, so {P} grows to about {comp10}. Most people guess lower.
t2.formula: Simple interest = principal × rate × years. Write the rate as a decimal. Example: ₹2,000 at 5% for 4 years is 2,000 × 0.05 × 4 = ₹400.
q3.prompt: With simple interest only, how much interest does {P} earn in {yrs} years at {rate}? Type a number in rupees.
q3.hint: Original money times the rate times the years.
q4.prompt: The compound garden ends higher than the simple one. How many rupees more is that, the interest on interest? Type a number in rupees.
q4.hint: Compound value minus simple value. Simple value is the original money plus the simple interest.
q4.explain: The compound garden reached {comp10}. The simple one reached {P} plus {interestS}. The gap is {extra}.
t3.title: Fast-forward
t3.define: The gap between the gardens does not grow evenly. It grows faster each year. Time is the strongest lever.
t3.formula: Compound amount = principal × (1 + rate)^years. The small raised number means multiply (1 + rate) by itself that many times. Example: ₹2,000 at 5% for 2 years is 2,000 × 1.05 × 1.05 = ₹2,205.
t3.rule72: Rule of 72: divide 72 by the yearly rate, written as a plain number, to estimate the years to double. Example: at 6% it takes about 72 ÷ 6 = 12 years.
t3.explore: Open the lab. Set the years to {yrsLong} and compare the two gardens.
q5.prompt: In the lab, what is the compound garden worth after {yrsLong} years? Type a number in rupees.
q5.hint: Read the compound value in the lab at {yrsLong} years.
q5.explain: {P} at {rate} a year for {yrsLong} years becomes about {comp20}.
q6.prompt: Use the Rule of 72. At {rate} a year, about how many years does money take to double? Type a number.
q7.prompt: As the years go on, what happens to the gap between the compound and simple gardens?
q7.opt.a: It grows bigger, and faster each year
q7.hint: Compare the gap at 10 years with the gap at {yrsLong} years in the lab.
q7.explain: Interest on interest keeps growing, so the gap widens faster each year.
t4.title: Start early
t4.hook: Asha and Dev each save {monthly} a month until age {stop}. Asha starts at age {ageE}. Dev starts at age {ageL}. Your mission: see what ten years does.
t4.explore: Open the lab. Set the starting age to {ageE} and note the result. Then set it to {ageL}.
q8.prompt: In the lab, what is Asha's money worth at age {stop} if she starts at {ageE}? Type a number in rupees.
q8.hint: Set the starting age to {ageE} and read the value at the end.
q8.explain: Saving {monthly} a month for {yearsE} years at {rateM} grows to about {earlyFV}.
q9.prompt: What is Dev's money worth at age {stop} if he starts at {ageL}? Type a number in rupees.
q9.hint: Set the starting age to {ageL} and read the value at the end.
q9.explain: Saving {monthly} a month for {yearsL} years grows to about {lateFV}.
q10.prompt: How many more rupees did Asha put in than Dev? Type a number in rupees.
q10.hint: Read what each of them put in, and subtract.
q10.explain: Asha put in {putEarly} and Dev put in {putLate}, so Asha put in {morePut} more.
q11.prompt: Dev says: starting ten years later is almost the same. What is the problem?
q11.opt.a: The extra ten years of growth are worth far more than the extra money Asha put in
q11.opt.b: Nothing, ten years makes almost no difference
q11.fb.b: Look at the two end values. Asha put in a little more but ends with far more, because her money had ten more years to grow.
q11.hint: Compare the extra money Asha put in with the gap between the end values.
q11.explain: Early money has more years to earn interest on interest. Starting early is worth far more than the extra rupees put in.
